author: Houston Republic
title: Houston Cougars men's golf selected for NCAA Bermuda Run Regional
text:
The University of Houston Men’s Golf program will compete in the NCAA Bermuda Run Regional as the #11 seed, according to a May 6 announcement. This marks the sixth consecutive season and the 26th time in school history that Houston has participated in NCAA Regional play.
The regional event will be hosted by Wake Forest at Bermuda Run Country Club. The Cougars are set to face teams including top-seeded Virginia, Mississippi, Pepperdine, Georgia Tech, USC, host Wake Forest, Mississippi State, Little Rock, NC State, Kentucky, Richmond, Navy and Presbyterian. Individual competitors from other schools such as Maryland and Western Carolina will also participate.
Head Coach Jonathan Dismuke has led Houston into postseason play for the twelfth time during his seventeen-year tenure. The top five teams from each regional site and the leading individual not on a qualifying team will advance to the NCAA Championships scheduled for May 29 through June 3 at Omni La Costa Resort and Spa in Carlsbad, California.
NCAA Regionals are set to take place from May 18-20 across six sites nationwide: Athens (Georgia), Bryan (Texas), Columbus (Ohio), Corvallis (Oregon), Marana (Arizona) and Bermuda Run (North Carolina). Dismuke and his team watched Wednesday’s selection show from their clubhouse at Golf Club of Houston in Humble.
This season saw Houston post eight Top-Five team finishes with championships at both the Argent Financial Classic and Border Olympics. Senior Hudson Weibel led individually with a scoring average of 70.57 over twenty-two rounds of par or lower; he became the first Cougar since 2013-14 to win three or more tournaments in one season. Junior Grant Doggett secured an individual title at Bayou City Collegiate Classic while junior Chi Chun Chen ranked third on the team with sixteen rounds of par or lower.
Historically, Houston has earned eight Top-Five finishes in regional play and won its only regional title in San Antonio during 1998. Four players have previously claimed medalist honors while fourteen have achieved Top-10 individual results.
